title: Topic 2.3: Crop Pest and Disease Control

pages.lesson:
LESSON: CROP PEST AND DISEASE CONTROL

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Food Production Processes
Topic 2.3: Crop Pest and Disease Control

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Crop Pest and Disease Control. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CROP PEST AND DISEASE CONTROL
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Crop Pest and Disease Control helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT PLANTS
Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.
Without water and light, most seedlings wilt.

PART 1: Identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Crop Pest and Disease Control” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Crop Pest and Disease Control is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.

Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Crop Pest and Disease Control” around your school. (skill: identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Crop Pest and Disease Control to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Crop Pest and Disease Control from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Crop Pest and Disease Control: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Crop Pest and Disease Control?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases?
2. How can we control pests and diseases affecting crops?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Crop Pest and Disease Control means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vegetable crops attacked by pests and diseases.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
